summary: Ephemeral GitHub App private-key rotation causes self-hosted runner registration and release jobs to 401/pend
summary_long: During scheduled rotation of the GitHub App private key used by the runner-manager service account, some self-hosted runner registration and release pipelines started failing with 401s against the GitHub API. The failure window impacted nightly and release workflows for multiple repos and blocked a customer-facing release job for ~45 minutes.
impact: Several release and nightly CI jobs across repos using self-hosted runners in prod-us-west failed to start or remained stuck in 'pending' state. One release pipeline for the public-sdk repo could not complete, delaying a hotfix deploy. Estimated user impact: internal release delays; no external customer-facing outage but delayed delivery.
steps_to_reproduce:
1) Trigger a new release workflow on a repo that uses self-hosted runners registered via the runner-manager service which authenticates to GitHub using the GitHub App private key.
2) Observe runner-manager attempting to refresh installation tokens and runner registration tokens.
3) After private-key rotation, observe GitHub API returning 401/Bad credentials for token exchange calls.
4) Runners fail to register and jobs remain pending.
observed_logs: 2026-03-12T02:14:07Z runner-manager [token-refresh] ERROR GitHub token exchange failed: 401 Bad credentials - JWT invalid or expired
2026-03-12T02:14:08Z runner-manager [registration] WARN Runner registration refused: installation-token-fetch failed
2026-03-12T02:14:09Z release-ci [job-12345] INFO Job pending: waiting for runner registration (timeout 1800s)
2026-03-12T02:20:00Z opsbot INFO Detected spike in 'bad_credentials' errors from runner-manager; correlated with scheduled key rotation job
investigation_notes: 03/12 02:16 - Confirmed rotation job for GitHub App private key completed successfully in key-rotation service; new private key version present in vault.
03/12 02:17 - runner-manager logs show it continued using in-memory JWT signed with old key for ~30s after rotation; after that JWT generation started failing with 401s.
03/12 02:21 - Obtained GitHub App audit logs: GitHub rejected JWTs signed by old key once the org-level App keys were rotated.
03/12 02:28 - Discovered rotation flow updated vault secret path but runner-manager was reading the private key from cached mounted file on disk; cache invalidation not implemented in runner-manager.
03/12 02:35 - Temporary workaround applied: restarted runner-manager pods to force re-read of key from vault-mounted file; registration resumed.

Root cause hypothesis: runner-manager caches the App private key on startup and relies on a restart window to pick up key rotation. Rotation job replaced the key in vault but did not trigger runner-manager reload; this caused a transient window where JWTs were signed with a revoked/old key and GitHub rejected them.
root_cause: Automation rotated the GitHub App private key in Vault, but runner-manager uses an on-disk cached copy and does not hot-reload keys. The rotation job did not trigger a rolling restart of runner-manager instances. As a result, JWTs signed with the old key were rejected by GitHub immediately after rotation, causing token exchange and runner registration calls to 401.
workaround: Restart runner-manager deployment to force reload of the new private key from Vault. For urgent releases, run a manual restart of runner-manager pods in prod-us-west until automated rotation workflow is updated.
resolution: Applied emergency fix: restarted all runner-manager pods in prod-us-west at 2026-03-12T02:36Z which allowed services to read the new private key and successfully exchange JWTs for installation tokens. Release pipeline resumed and the blocked hotfix was deployed. Follow-up PRs merged to automate restart during rotation and add hot-reload.
follow_up_actions: Create an automated hook in the key-rotation pipeline to trigger a rolling restart of runner-manager deployments when the GitHub App private key changes (PR #4182)
Implement key hot-reload in runner-manager so new private keys can be picked up without restarts (issue: infra#5621)
Add pre-rotation checks that mark App rotations as "safe-to-rotate" only after verifying at least one runner-manager instance has successfully authenticated with a test JWT
Add monitoring alert for >5% rate of 401s from runner-manager to GitHub within a 5-minute window
Update runbook: 'github-app-key-rotation' with explicit safe-rotation steps and rollback instructions (confluence: /display/OPS/GitHub+App+Key+Rotation)
Postmortem scheduled: 2026-03-15 in #incidents; include notes about change management and automation coverage
